system_description.narrative_title: Hormuz blockade and regional attacks choking global oil supply
system_description.narrative_summary: An escalating standoff centered on Iran’s control over the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and increased U.S. naval pressure, is disrupting crude flows, raising prices and forcing rerouting of exports and refinery adjustments. Treated as an open system, physical flows (tankers, pipelines, inventories), signals (diplomacy, military actions, forecasts), and market responses (prices, insurance, demand destruction) exchange matter, energy and information across boundaries, producing feedbacks that deepen supply shortfalls and prompt policy and commercial countermeasures. Concrete actors include Iran, the U.S., Gulf producers, Houthis and oil firms; systemic variables include chokepoint throughput, spare capacity, shipping/insurance premia and market expectations. Ongoing strikes, talks, spills and lease/production decisions act as catalysts that continually reshape system trajectories.
system_description.scope: Maritime oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz and adjacent seas, regional military/naval operations and diplomatic negotiations affecting transit, global crude supply balances and prices, rerouting infrastructure (pipelines, alternate export routes), refining and storage capacity, shipping/insurance markets and strategic reserves.
system_description.super_system: Global energy–economy–security system (world oil markets embedded within international trade, finance and geopolitics).
adjacent_subsystems: Global shipping, logistics and marine insurance
Downstream refining, storage and petrochemical capacity
Regional Middle East security and diplomatic architecture
evidence_headlines: U.S. oil rises above $83 a barrel as Iran says Strait of Hormuz won't open until conditions are met
Hormuz shipping traffic falls to one-week low amid hostilities
IEA slashes 2026 supply forecast as Hormuz reopening remains elusive
Saudi Red Sea oil exports go dark as Houthi attack threat grows
US says it can keep naval blockade on Iran 'indefinitely,' vows more economic pressure
Gulf oil spill fast becoming worst in years, agencies warn

variables.name: Chokepoint throughput
variables.description: The volumetric rate of crude and oil-product cargo (barrels/day) transiting strategic maritime chokepoints.

variables.name: Tanker transit rate
variables.description: The number of oil tankers and related cargo vessels passing through key sea lanes per unit time.

variables.name: Spare production capacity
variables.description: The volume of additional oil production that can be brought online within a defined short-to-medium timeframe.

variables.name: Global supply gap
variables.description: The net difference between globally available oil supply and aggregate demand at prevailing conditions.

variables.name: Refinery utilization
variables.description: The proportion of global refining capacity that is actively processing crude into products at a given time.

variables.name: Commercial inventories
variables.description: The aggregated level of commercial crude and product stocks held in storage facilities and terminals.

variables.name: Marine insurance premia
variables.description: The average war-risk, hull and other voyage insurance premium levels charged for tanker voyages in affected waters.

variables.name: Shipping freight rate
variables.description: The freight cost per ton (or per barrel) for transporting crude and refined products by sea.

variables.name: Maritime interdiction intensity
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of naval and quasi‑naval operations that obstruct or control maritime transit.

variables.name: Hostile incident rate
variables.description: The rate of armed attacks, strikes, seizures or hostile events directed at shipping and maritime infrastructure.

variables.name: Export rerouting share
variables.description: The proportion of export volumes diverted from primary sea routes to alternative pipelines, terminals or passages.

variables.name: Average transit delay
variables.description: The mean additional time incurred per voyage due to inspections, rerouting, congestion or security measures.

variables.name: Benchmark crude price
variables.description: The prevailing market reference price level for crude oil (e.g., international benchmark) in currency per barrel.

variables.name: Market supply expectations
variables.description: The prevailing collective expectation in markets about future supply–demand balance and tightness over the forecasting horizon.

variables.name: Demand destruction rate
variables.description: The rate at which oil consumption declines in response to price increases, economic slowdown or access constraints.

variables.name: Strategic reserve drawdown rate
variables.description: The rate at which government and strategic reserves are released or withdrawn into the market.

catalysts.title: U.S. indefinite naval blockade operations
catalysts.description: Sustained U.S. naval blockade posture and enforcement actions in and around the Strait of Hormuz that constrain shipping access.
catalysts.rationale: "US says it can keep naval blockade on Iran 'indefinitely'"; multiple reports of US firing on ships enforcing blockade.

catalysts.title: Stalled Iran–US talks keep Hormuz closed
catalysts.description: Diplomatic deadlock leaves Iran's conditions unmet and the Strait effectively closed, prolonging restricted oil flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Iran says Strait of Hormuz won't open until conditions are met"; "Hormuz reopening remains elusive", IEA warnings.

catalysts.title: Escalation of Houthi attacks in Red Sea
catalysts.description: Increased frequency/severity of Houthi strikes on ships and infrastructure in the Red Sea and nearby approaches, prompting reroutes and strikes.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: Houthi attacks kill crew, hit Saudi facilities; U.S. strikes container ships; Red Sea threats grow.

catalysts.title: Ship oil leak and salvage off Oman
catalysts.description: Ongoing salvage and cleanup of a leaking vessel off Oman that could temporarily disrupt nearby transits and raise local risk perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: "Risk firm Ambrey working to salvage ship spewing oil off Oman"; salvors working to secure ship leaking oil off Oman.

catalysts.title: Saudi expansion of Mediterranean pipeline exports
catalysts.description: Saudi and Gulf producers accelerate use and expansion of Mediterranean routing to avoid Red Sea/Hormuz vulnerabilities, shifting flows and congestion.
catalysts.rationale: "Saudi Arabia ramps up oil exports through Mediterranean pipeline to avoid attacks in Red Sea"; Saudi Red Sea exports go dark.

catalysts.title: Major oil firms resume Venezuelan activity
catalysts.description: Oil majors' tentative return and deals in Venezuela begin to restart production and investment, adding potential incremental supply over months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "BP joins Big Oil return to post‑Maduro Venezuela"; majors partnering on Venezuelan development.

catalysts.title: Accelerated North Sea well closures
catalysts.description: Regulator-driven or operator-initiated faster well closures in the North Sea reduce near-term output, tightening supply balances.
catalysts.rationale: "North Sea oil producers told to speed up well closures" — FT/Reuters coverage indicates output cuts ahead.
